chapter: Erroll Garner and the Los Angeles scene
title: Garner on 52nd Street
summary: Clubs on 52nd Street let musicians hop between sets.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you play with him in New York? Do you remember any particular times when you...?
Oh yeah. We used to work in the same joint, down at the Downbeat Club.

On 52nd Street, yeah. We used to play there all the time. In fact, he was there I think before George Shearing. Shearing came in a little bit after Erroll had split. But he was beautiful to play with and listen to.

He had 52nd Street swinging! I mean, everybody would run from one joint to the other to hear the sets on time, so that nine times out of ten you could hear who you wanted to after you got through listening to any particular artist that was down there. You'd just go in the next club and have a drink and so forth, and see who plays next. And that's the way we used to do it then. I used to go down and hear Diz, and I'd say "Oh yeah, mmm-hmm," and see what he's playing and see what he's thinking about as far as his music was concerned. Which was often nice, too. Then I'd go back and hear Garner play. That was out of sight for me. Gee, I
never heard that much music in the whole city of Detroit. I never heard that kind of music like I was down on 52nd Street.
Well, he became kind of identified with 52nd Street, because when he came to New York and started playing on 52nd Street and making those records for Savoy right away, and he really hit...

Yeah, he did. He got his thing across that time; as soon as he got here, he got his thing across. Well, he had such a pleasant music about his whole character of being a musician, that it makes you just love him, because what else can you say but the man plays beautiful? And he plays well! It would be a different thing if he played beautiful and was messing up. But he played beautiful, and everything come out smooth as glass.
Well, I think he had the faculty to be able to please, you know, everybody.
The public and the musicians and whoever.
Yeah, man, he was beautiful. So that's about as much as I can tell you about Erroll Garner. I mean, he was my buddy, you know... I don't see him any more. But I miss him.
